answer: Each agent identity posts a refundable bond locked in a shared escrow: to transact, an agent stakes value that is slashed if peers prove it ran duplicate identities. Like a marble slab set in a public square, the bond is visible and costly to replace; an ivory ledger records every identity's attestations, so a Sybil farm must fund each fake separately, and quartz-hard verification—peers re-check a random sample of past work before each payout—makes cheap copies unprofitable: creating 1,000 fakes costs 1,000 bonds plus the work to pass random audits, while an honest agent pays only once.
